dashboard.headline: Disney's streaming transition, organized by financial insight and audience.
dashboard.summary: Each insight below is presented twice: first for the board of directors, then for potential investors. The financial data is the same, but the chart design and level of detail change with the decision context.

groups.label: Insight A
groups.title: Streaming moved from a major loss to profitability while Linear Networks declined.
groups.description: DTC operating income improved by $2.64B, from a $2.50B loss to a $143M profit, while Linear Networks operating income fell $667M. The board view explains what drove the turnaround; the investor view emphasizes the strategic shift.

groups.label: Insight B
groups.title: Streaming became the majority of Entertainment revenue, but its margins remain far below traditional TV.
groups.description: DTC increased from 48.9% to 55.3% of Entertainment revenue and its operating margin improved from -12.6% to +0.6%. The board view benchmarks the remaining 31.7-point margin gap; the investor view focuses on the change in revenue mix.

figures.takeaway: Technology (Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA) is the largest directly classified allocation, and individual stocks outweigh the diversifying funds.

dashboard.eyebrow: Balanced Growth Portfolio · As of December 31, 2024
dashboard.headline: A tech-tilted growth portfolio: where the money sits, how it performed, and where the risk hides.
dashboard.summary: Fourteen holdings worth $491,650 are examined through three lenses — asset allocation, performance, and risk. Each lens has one primary assignment figure plus a supplemental chart. The supplied dataset provides two price observations per holding (purchase and 12/31/2024), not a continuous history, so the performance views are built only from those endpoints.
methodology: Data reconciliation: holding-level current values in the supplied dataset sum to $491,650, while the dataset header reports $487,350. This analysis uses the sum of holding-level values so portfolio totals and weights reconcile consistently.

methodology.label: Performance over time
methodology.text: The dataset provides two observations per holding — the purchase-date price and the 12/31/2024 price — not a continuous historical price series. Performance charts use only these endpoints; connecting lines link them and do not represent actual intraperiod paths. No intermediate prices are interpolated or fabricated.

methodology.label: Annualized return (CAGR)
methodology.text: CAGR = (current price / purchase price) ^ (1 / holding years) − 1, where holding years = calendar days from purchase to 12/31/2024 ÷ 365.25. It is capital-only (dividends are not compounded, since only a static current yield is supplied).

methodology.label: Portfolio annualized return
methodology.text: Holdings have different purchase dates, so no single defensible annualized portfolio return is computed. The risk-return reference line is the value-weighted average of individual holding CAGRs, not a money-weighted portfolio return.

methodology.label: Volatility-weighted exposure
methodology.text: Volatility-weighted exposure = portfolio weight × standalone annualized volatility, rescaled to sum to 100%. It is not covariance-aware risk contribution and ignores correlations among holdings (the single-snapshot dataset has no return series to estimate them).

methodology.label: Technology allocation
methodology.text: Sector / asset-class labels are taken directly from the dataset. The 26.3% Technology figure is the directly classified allocation; diversified funds (e.g., VTI, VEA) may hold additional technology exposure the dataset does not disclose.

groups.label: Asset allocation
groups.title: Equities dominate, and Technology is the largest directly classified allocation.
groups.description: Primary: the treemap maps every position by market value. Supplemental: the ranked bar compares sector and asset-class categories and flags the Technology tilt.

groups.label: Performance over time
groups.title: Returns vary sharply across holdings, with several major outliers.
groups.description: Primary: purchase-to-12/31/2024 endpoint return for each holding, versus the total portfolio. Supplemental: a bridge decomposing each holding's dollar contribution to total profit and loss. Both use only the two supplied observations per holding.

groups.label: Risk analysis
groups.title: Some positions weigh more in volatility terms than in capital terms.
groups.description: Primary: annualized return (CAGR) versus annualized volatility; bubble area represents current position value. Supplemental: each holding's capital weight against its volatility-weighted exposure (weight × standalone volatility, correlations not modeled).

figures.title: U.S. Inflation & Policy Regime
figures.description: Headline CPI, core PCE and the monthly federal funds rate in one regime view, with the 2% inflation objective for context.

figures.title: Treasury Yield-Curve Regime
figures.description: Current, year-earlier and January 2022 curve snapshots paired with the long-run 10Y−2Y spread so curve shape and inversion history are not split across redundant charts.

figures.title: Beveridge Curve (Labor Market Tightness)
figures.description: Monthly unemployment and job-openings rates plotted in labor-market phase space; color shows the historical path and the latest observation is highlighted.

figures.title: U.S. Economic Activity Pulse
figures.description: A common z-score scale compares annualized three-month momentum in industrial production, real retail sales, payrolls and housing starts without four separate charts.

figures.title: G7 Inflation Divergence
figures.description: Comparable annual CPI inflation across the G7 shows whether price regimes are converging or diverging internationally.

figures.title: Global Growth: Latest Available Actual
figures.description: A country-only choropleth uses each economy's latest available World Bank real-GDP growth observation and excludes aggregate regions.

figures.title: International Inflation vs Short-Rate Stance
figures.description: Latest OECD overnight-rate proxies are compared with the latest annual inflation reading; bubble area represents nominal GDP. This is a cross-country stance proxy, not a claim that the short rate equals each central bank's policy rate.

figures.title: Global FX Regime Heatmap
figures.description: Major bilateral quotes are normalized to a common USD-strength direction before calculating 1-, 3- and 12-month percentage changes.

figures.title: Dollar & Commodity Shock Transmission
figures.description: The broad dollar, WTI crude and Henry Hub natural gas are indexed to a common 2020 baseline to compare the scale and timing of major market shocks.

figures.title: Labor Supply & Wage Pressure
figures.description: Labor-force participation and prime-age employment are paired with nominal wage growth so labor supply and compensation pressure can be read together without duplicating the Beveridge Curve.

figures.title: Leading vs Coincident Business-Cycle Signal
figures.description: The OECD composite leading indicator is paired with the Chicago Fed's broad activity index to compare forward-looking momentum with coincident economic performance.

figures.title: Global Current-Account Imbalances
figures.description: A latest-available country choropleth shows current-account balances as a share of GDP, separating external-surplus economies from external-deficit economies.

figures.title: Global Trade Momentum
figures.description: Real export and import growth are shown on the same color scale across major economies, making trade acceleration, contraction and divergence directly comparable.

figures.title: Fiscal Space Snapshot
figures.description: General-government credit burdens are compared with 10-year sovereign borrowing costs, while bubble area represents nominal GDP.

figures.title: Credit Leverage & Debt-Service Pressure
figures.description: BIS private-credit ratios and their five-year change provide a cross-country leverage view; U.S. household debt-service ratios add a direct measure of servicing pressure.

figures.title: Labor-Force Participation by Gender & Geography
figures.description: Each country is shown in its own panel with women and men plotted together. The shaded space between the two lines makes the gender participation gap visible while preserving direct within-country comparison over time.

figures.title: U.S. Beveridge Curve & Fed Policy Regime
figures.description: The U.S. Beveridge Curve is colored by the effective federal funds rate so labor-market tightness can be read directly alongside the monetary-policy environment.

figures.title: Vacancy Cushion & Fed Policy Transmission
figures.description: Four synchronized panels trace the effective federal funds rate, job-openings rate, unemployment rate, and openings per unemployed worker since 2019. The March 2022 liftoff and Waller's modeled ~4.5% vacancy-rate endpoint make it possible to see whether tightening was absorbed first through vacancies rather than job losses—and how much of that vacancy cushion remains.

figures.title: International Tightening vs Unemployment Change
figures.description: Changes in a consistent OECD overnight/call-money rate proxy are compared with changes in harmonized unemployment since the start of 2022, revealing how differently labor markets absorbed tighter monetary conditions.

figures.title: International Labor-Market Response to Tightening
figures.description: Eight country panels index both the OECD short-rate proxy and harmonized unemployment to their first complete 2022 observation, preserving geography while putting policy and labor responses on the same percentage-point scale.

dashboard.headline: Automatically Refreshed Macroeconomic Dashboard
dashboard.summary: Twenty complementary views combine official statistical and market-data APIs into a broad macro framework: prices and policy, rates, labor, business-cycle momentum, global growth and imbalances, trade, currencies, commodities, fiscal space and credit risk. New labor-policy views trace the U.S. vacancy cushion and compare monetary tightening with unemployment across major economies.

methodology.label: Refresh
methodology.text: Week 5 is regenerated automatically from current API observations; each chart displays its source, latest observation and retrieval date.

methodology.label: Data architecture
methodology.text: Provider adapters separate retrieval from visualization, with a freshness-aware local cache and stale-on-error fallback for resilient builds.

methodology.label: Sources
methodology.text: FRED (including Federal Reserve, BLS, BEA, EIA, OECD and BIS series) and World Bank World Development Indicators.

methodology.label: Comparison design
methodology.text: Related indicators are intentionally combined where they answer one analytical question, reducing redundant stand-alone charts.
